svg.title: Dual blood supply of the retina

g.title: Inner retina (inner two-thirds): fed by the central retinal artery
Outer retina and photoreceptors (outer third): no retinal vessels, fed by the choroid
Ophthalmic artery (passes behind the optic nerve in this view)
Sclera (continuous with the dural sheath of the optic nerve)
Optic nerve (retinal nerve fibres turn into it at the disc)
Optic disc with the physiological cup
Oxygen and nutrients diffuse from the choriocapillaris to the photoreceptors
Retinal capillary plexuses (superficial and deep) in the inner retina
Central retinal vein and retinal veins
Central retinal artery: enters the optic nerve and branches over the inner retina
Short posterior ciliary arteries: pierce the sclera to feed the choroid
Choroidal veins draining to a vortex vein
Boundary between the retinal and choroidal supply
